title: Console rendering resilience: graceful degradation & parity for charts, tables, and modals
creator: Ava Chen
description: Improve cross-browser visual parity and graceful degradation across the Redwood Console for primary surfaces (dashboards charts, tabular lists, and modals). Deliver a set of responsive breakpoints, rendering fallbacks for Safari/Firefox edge-cases, and interaction patterns for touch/keyboard that preserve data density and observability signals. This ticket produces final specs, interactive prototypes, and a prioritized implementation checklist for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Charts render consistently (axis alignment, tick density, tooltip placement) across Chromium, Safari, and Firefox at 320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440 widths
Tables maintain header stickiness + accessible keyboard navigation when virtualized (no clipping/visual jump) across supported browsers
Modals preserve stacking context and focus-trap behavior with no scroll-jank or layout shift on mobile browsers
Fallbacks defined for browsers that lack ResizeObserver or full canvas/SVG performance (clear decision path: use SVG where available, rasterize selectively)
Design handoff artifacts (Figma frames, redlines, token mappings) uploaded and a PRD created linking acceptance tests and QA checklist
review_feedback: PM @Miguel Torres: prioritize table header stickiness over fancy chart compression for 1024 width (customer dashboards rely on persistent column labels).
Eng @Priya Nambiar: avoid large runtime polyfills; prefer feature-detect + progressive enhancement. Suggests a ResizeObserver fallback using polling only for legacy Safari versions.
Accessibility @Jordan Blake: tooltip-on-focus must be reachable via keyboard and not rely solely on hover; request ARIA live region for chart updates.
Design Director @Riley Park: reduce visual density at mobile widths by collapsing secondary metrics into a stacked summary row rather than truncating labels.
tasks: Finalize breakpoint token table and density rules for 320/375/412/768/1024/1440
Produce redlines for chart axis spacing, tick density, and tooltip offset per breakpoint
Define rendering strategy: SVG-first for charts, canvas fallback heuristic for >1000 series points
Document table virtualization guidelines and header sticky implementation constraints
Create modal z-index and focus-trap spec including edge-case flows (nested modals, confirm prompts)
Handoff package to ENG with prioritized tickets and QA checklist
qa_checklist: Verify chart axis alignment across Chrome/Safari/Firefox at listed breakpoints
Test tooltips on desktop (hover/keyboard) and touch (tap/long-press) for placement and accessibility
Confirm table header stickiness during virtualized scroll, and no content flashing on mount
Validate modal open/close focus trap, return focus, and scroll prevention on iOS Safari
Run Lighthouse accessibility audit and log outstanding issues
Cross-browser visual diff snapshots for dashboard snapshot on PR

decisions: Adopt SVG-first rendering for charts to preserve crisp axis/text rendering; switch to canvas rasterization only when data points exceed 1200 within a single series and when browser reports GPU constraints.
Implement ResizeObserver with a guarded fallback: small interval polling (200ms) on browsers without RO support, behind a feature-flag for early rollout.

Use CSS position:sticky for table headers with containment heuristics to prevent paint storms. For legacy browsers where sticky behaves inconsistently, provide a JS-driven fallback that toggles a 'stuck' class.
Modals will use a single stacking root managed by the console shell; nested modal flows will be flattened into confirm flows to avoid z-index escalation bugs.
Tooltips will appear on focus and hover; touch will show a tap-to-open tooltip with a small close affordance. All tooltips will include aria-describedby where appropriate.
